No, that's not what Mac said.
If you own an RPG Maker, you have the rights to use the assets from that RPG Maker in any game-making engine you own.
The same is automatically true of
edits
of those assets.
What Mac said is you need to look up who made the bases that you used to see if that author
added
any terms to their work, saying it could only be used in RPG Maker games. Most people do not do that.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
To clarify the background a bit:
for decades the licence for all makers and all their resources stated that those resources and their edits could only be used in a game software that was part of the RPG Maker series.
And all people that distributed edits of them honored that by stating the same.
However a short while ago GGG changed that licence, allowing the both the originals and their edits to be used in any game making software.
Older Resource sites mostly have not changed their terms yet however, and you cannot determine on your own if something is only an edit from a maker resource, or if the artist has done more that might still be restricted by other licences.
So when you get to one such site, you can either obey the licence as given there OR ask the artist to consider updating his licence to reflect the newest RM-licences.
And if the artist cannot be found then you'll hjave to follow the old licences.
